environment.description: Same NestJS service on ECS Fargate behind an internal ALB (scheme: internal) in a private subnet. Ingress is controlled via a Network Load Balancer with a PrivateLink endpoint service. The NLB has a target group with proxy_protocol_v2 enabled and a listener-level security policy. Access is restricted through a combination of: (1) VPC endpoint policy on the consumer side limiting principal to specific AWS account IDs, (2) the NLB security group allows inbound TCP/443 only from CIDR 10.200.0.0/16 and 172.16.32.0/21 which correspond to the three known internal service VPCs peered via Transit Gateway, (3) AWS Network Firewall stateful rule group with a Suricata-compatible rule inspecting TLS SNI and dropping connections not matching the internal service hostname pattern *.internal.corp.example.com. The combination means only traffic originating from known internal service VPCs with valid endpoint policies can reach the ALB. Timing attacks require thousands of precisely-timed requests from a network-adjacent position; the multi-hop path through PrivateLink + NLB + internal ALB introduces 8-15ms of variable jitter per request, and the restricted CIDR means an attacker cannot position themselves on a low-latency path to the service.

config.network_firewall_rule: drop tls any any -> any any (tls.sni; content:!'.internal.corp.example.com'; sid:1000001; rev:1;)
